1#main: One who acquires a slave — it is forbidden to maintain him uncircumcised, and his immersion, blessing, circumcision, and all laws of male and female slaves. And it contains 85 seifim. It is a positive mitzvah for the master to circumcise his slaves; if the master transgressed and did not circumcise them, beit din is commanded to circumcise him — whether a slave born in an Israelite's house or one bought from a gentile; he is obligated to circumcise him, and they are circumcised only by day. A house-born slave is circumcised on the eighth day; an acquisition with money is circumcised on the day he was acquired — even if he bought him on the day he was born, he circumcises him that day: {Rama: (If one bought the maidservant and another bought the fetus, they circumcise one (Tur); all the more if one bought a maidservant and her child with her, they circumcise one) (Beit Yosef).} And there is acquisition with money circumcised on the eighth, and house-born circumcised on the day he was born: How so? He bought a maidservant and her fetus with her and she gave birth — behold he is circumcised on the eighth; and even though he bought the fetus by itself, behold the fetus is acquisition with money since he bought his mother before birth — circumcised on the eighth. He bought a maidservant for her pregnancy, or bought a maidservant on condition not to immerse her for servitude — even though born in his domain: {Rama: (and she conceived in his house) (Tur)} — circumcised on the day he was born, for this newborn is as if acquisition with money alone and as if acquired today, for his mother is not in the category of Israelite maidservants so the son be house-born; and if his mother immersed after she gave birth, behold he is circumcised on the eighth.
2#main: Just as circumcision of sons overrides Shabbat, so circumcision of slaves who are circumcised on the eighth overrides Shabbat — except house-born and acquisition with money whose mother did not immerse until she gave birth, for even though they are circumcised on the eighth they do not override Shabbat.
3#main: A slave taken from a gentile — they say to him: Do you wish to enter the category of Israelite slaves and be among the fit, or not? If he wishes, they inform him of fundamentals of faith and some light and severe mitzvot and their punishments and rewards, as they inform a convert; and they immerse him like a convert and inform him while he is in the water: {Rama: (And the slave blesses on immersion, not the master) (Nimmukei Yosef, chapter HaChalitzah, Maggid Mishneh chapter 13 of Forbidden Relations).}
4#main: If he bought an adult slave from a gentile and the slave did not wish to be circumcised — they roll with him for all twelve months; beyond that it is forbidden to maintain him uncircumcised, but he returns and sells him to a gentile: {Rama: And specifically where he bought him in order to convert him to slavery; but if he stipulated explicitly not to circumcise him (Tur, Mordechai chapter HaChalitzah, Rambam chapter 1 of Milah, chapter 14 of Forbidden Relations, Raavad there); and likewise in these lands where it is forbidden to convert any gentile — it is as if he stipulated with him not to circumcise, and permitted to maintain him uncircumcised as long as he wishes (same in Mordechai there and Rabbeinu Yerucham); and so is the plain custom.}
5#main: If he circumcised his slave and immersed him against his will for servitude — he did nothing: {Rama: (Nevertheless, if he did willingly and practiced slave mitzvot, he can free him afterward against his will) (Tur).}
6#main: A minor slave or imbecile — they immerse him on beit din's understanding.
7#main: When the slave is freed, he needs immersion afterward before three; and he need not accept mitzvot and be informed of fundamentals of faith, for they already informed him when he immersed for servitude.
8#main: A gentile slave whom his master circumcised and he returned to gentile ways, and sold him to a gentile and an Israelite bought him from him — behold he is like an apostate Israelite and needs no immersion, only lashes: {Rama: (And some say nevertheless ab initio they return and immerse him in a higher sense) (Nimmukei Yosef, chapter HaChalitzah).}
9#main: One who buys a slave from a gentile — the body is not acquired until he immerses him for servitude; therefore if he preceded and immersed for the sake of freedom, behold he is free: {Rama: And nevertheless he must pay his master the money he gave for him (Nimmukei Yosef, chapter HaChalitzah, Maggid Mishneh chapter 13, in the name of Ritva's teacher, Rabbeinu Yerucham, and see Even HaEzer); and if beit din or another immersed him for freedom, he must pay if he knew he was this one's slave (there in Beit Yosef); but if they did not immerse him but advised the slave to immerse for freedom — exempt (Teshuvat Rashba, not like Beit Yosef who wrote Rabbeinu Yerucham disagrees; see Bach).} Therefore one must impose some labor upon him while still in the water so he appear a slave, lest he precede and say he immerses for freedom; but a gentile who sells himself to an Israelite acquires his body immediately and cannot precede to immerse for freedom.
10#main: When do we say this? When buying a slave from a gentile the body is not acquired when that gentile acquired the slave because he sold himself; but if he acquired him by law of the kingdom that acquires the body for him and an Israelite bought from him — if he preceded and immersed for freedom, he did not acquire himself as free.
11#main: One who has a maidservant not yet immersed for servitude — another may not immerse her without the master's permission: {Rama: For perhaps the master does not wish to immerse her for servitude, for he prefers she remain a gentile who can do his needs on Shabbat; he can also sell her to a gentile; and if another transgressed and immersed her, he must pay the master for damage (Rabbeinu Yerucham netiv 13).}
12#main: One who circumcises slaves blesses, Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to circumcise slaves; and if he circumcises another's slaves, he blesses on circumcision of slaves; and afterward blesses, Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to circumcise slaves and to draw covenant blood from them, etc., Blessed are You, Lord, Who cuts the covenant.
13#main: One must cover his nakedness at the time of blessing since he is adult.
14#main: A Hebrew slave applies only when yovel applies; and this is for acquiring his body; but for other laws of Hebrew slave — where he acquired him for his labor by law of the kingdom, such as captured in war and tax collectors sold him — an Israelite may buy him for his labor; and this slave may give his Israelite master the price of acquisition or his value, and the master's hand is on the bottom to take the lesser.
15#main: People who do not conduct properly — it is permitted to subdue them by force and enslave them.
16#main: A king who decreed that whoever does not pay the tax fixed per person shall be enslaved to whoever paid the tax for him — it is permitted to use him more than usual, but not as a full slave; and if he does not conduct properly, permitted to use him as a slave.
17#main: One who buys a gentile slave from an Israelite or gentile, and a gentile who sold himself to an Israelite or sold his sons and daughters — behold he is like a Canaanite slave, except one bought from a gentile — his body is not acquired except for labor, unless acquired by law of the kingdom (so implied from Tosafot and individual opinion per Rambam and Even HaEzer); and in all, as long as they did not immerse for servitude, his law is like a gentile for everything; and after immersion for servitude he is a slave obligated in mitzvot a woman is obligated in; and with this slave it is permitted to work him with rigor — even though the law is so, from piety and ways of wisdom a person should be merciful, not make his yoke heavy, not distress him, feed and give him drink of all food and drink, not disgrace him by hand or word, not increase shouting and anger, but speak gently, hear his claims.
18#main: A gentile king who made war, brought captives and sold them; and if he permitted anyone to go steal from a people he warred with, bring and sell for himself; and if his laws were that whoever does not pay tax is sold, or whoever does such-and-such or does not do is sold — behold his laws are valid laws, and a slave acquired under these laws is like a Canaanite slave for everything.
19#main: A woman acquires maidservants but not male slaves, even minors, because of suspicion.
20#main: The master can say to his slave: work with me and I will not sustain you; but my slaves are melog property (property like melog of the head — husband eats fruits and leaves principal, no dominion over this) — he is obligated to sustain them: {Rama: And some say this that he can say I will not sustain you applies when years are normal; but in famine year they do not have mercy on him; but he can say: go, your labor is for your sustenance, even if insufficient (Tur, Tosafot, Rosh, Rashba).}
21#main: One who cuts off his fellow's Canaanite slave's hand gives five things to the master; and the slave is sustained from charity even though the master takes Shabbat, for he can say work with me and I will not sustain you; healing — master gives for his healing; and if they assessed healing in five days and strong medicines healed in three, the master takes the advantage even if the slave suffered from strong medicines: {Rama: (And all the more if the master injured him — exempt) (Misharim 53; see seif 37).}
22#main: Whatever the slave acquires, his master acquires — whether found object or gift given him, whether from master or another — the other does not acquire except all goes to the master, body and produce; even if he said I give you on condition your master has no power — it is nothing unless he says I give you on condition you go out to freedom with it: {Rama: (Therefore he cannot receive a gift from his master, but from another for the master, and from master to another) (Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 5 of Laws of Slaves, Semag siman 86 positive mitzvah).}
23#main: A Canaanite slave — whether acquired while still gentile or after his master immersed him — is acquired by money, document, or chazakah, whether from gentile or Israelite; chazakah is using him, such as untying his shoe, putting on his shoe, taking his vessels to bathhouse, dressing, undressing, washing, anointing, or scraping him: {Rama: And specifically these for bodily service; but other work such as sewing his garments — no (Tur and see Even HaEzer).}
24#main: If the slave lifted for the master for use — acquired; if the master lifted for the slave — did not acquire.
25#main: Acquired by chalipin (exchange acquisition — exchanging what he gives in the corner of a garment); and by meshichah — he seized and drew him to himself; but if he called and he came — not acquired unless he is a minor.
